statement: In right triangle $FGH$, angle $H$ is the right angle and $\sin F = \frac{20}{29}$. What is the value of $\cos G$?

choices.misconception: I thought $\cos G$ was $1 - \sin F$, so I subtracted $\frac{20}{29}$ from 1.
I found the third side, 21, and gave $\cos F$, which uses the side next to $F$, instead of $\cos G$.
I found the third side, 21, and gave $\tan F = \frac{20}{21}$ instead of $\cos G$.

hints: The side opposite $F$ is the side adjacent to $G$. Compare the ratio for $\sin F$ with the ratio for $\cos G$.

solutions.reliable: With the right angle at $H$, the hypotenuse is $\overline{FG}$. Then $\sin F = \frac{\text{side opposite } F}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{GH}{FG}$ and $\cos G = \frac{\text{side adjacent to } G}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{GH}{FG}$. These are the same ratio, so $\cos G = \frac{20}{29}$.
solutions.elegant: Angles $F$ and $G$ are complementary, so $\cos G = \sin(90^\circ - G) = \sin F = \frac{20}{29}$.
